subject: Pricing exhibit: cushion / cascade anchoring - redlines
messages:
From: Maya Green <maya.green@acmecloud.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-08T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing exhibit redlines and packaging questions

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked the dedicated capacity examples. Attached are our annotated orderform and pricing exhibit (pricing_exhibit_v3.pdf, annotated_orderform.xlsx). We’ve flagged a few places where the current language on the pricing exhibit could create ambiguity for our finance team:

- Cushion / cascade anchoring: The exhibit references a "cushion" that cascades between SKUs but doesn’t define whether the cushion is applied at SKU level or aggregate account level. This materially changes our true-up exposure.
- Floor true-up timing: We need clarity on whether the floor is evaluated monthly or at quarter close for billing reconciliation.
- Packaging / SKU split: If we split consumption across bundled SKUs, we need a clear calculation to avoid double counting credits.

Can you route this to legal/ops and confirm whether Redwood is open to the attached suggested edits? We’d like to close pricing and get the PO in next week (PO-8891).

Also, is there a grace-window for the cushion that would apply during ramp months?

Best,
Maya Green
Head of Procurement, AcmeCloud

Attachments: annotated_orderform.xlsx (xlsx), pricing_exhibit_v3.pdf (pdf)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Maya Green <maya.green@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-08T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing exhibit redlines and packaging questions

Hi Maya — thanks for sending these over and for the clear annotations. I reviewed the attachment and put together a short summary of the open items + recommended approach (attached: naomi_response_markups.pdf). TL;DR: we can accept tightened language but want to preserve predictable economics for both sides.

Summary of outstanding items and our proposed direction:

1) Cushion / cascade anchoring
- Issue: ambiguous scope (SKU vs account aggregate).
- Redwood proposal: define "cushion" as an account-level buffer that is allocated pro rata to SKUs for reporting but not for increasing credit exposure. The cushion will only be applied after aggregate consumption exceeds the threshold in Exhibit A. This prevents fragmented cushions causing multiple small payouts across SKUs.

2) Floor true-up timing
- Issue: whether floor is evaluated monthly or quarterly.
- Redwood proposal: true-up at quarter close with monthly provisional statements. Quarter-end reconciliation is standard for our enterprise customers and aligns with billing cycles. If Acme requires monthly legal obligation, we’ll need to scope the administrative burden and potential fee to offset monthly reconciliation costs.

3) Packaging / SKU split calculation
- Issue: double counting when bundles unpack across usage categories.
- Redwood proposal: use the bundled SKU mapping in Appendix 2; allocation will be by primary consumption metric (tokens consumed in primary model) and we’ll include an anti-double-count clause.

Next steps: Ben and Laura — can you review the redline language I’ve sketched for Exhibit A and the new Appendix 2 language?

Maya — would you be available for a quick call Wednesday 2027-05-10 at 09:00 PT to walk through the edits? If that works we’ll bring final proposed contract language for a quick signoff.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Sales Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachment: naomi_response_markups.pdf (pdf)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-08T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Pricing exhibit redlines and packaging questions

Naomi / Laura — quick read and suggested edits below. I’m attaching a short clause proposal (legal_clause_proposal.docx) with tracked language. Key points:

- Cushion scope: change to "account-wide buffer" and add a definitional paragraph that the cushion does not create an additional payable credit unless the aggregate threshold is breached. This protects against per-SKU erosion.

- Grace-window: recommend a 45-day ramp grace period tied to the initial contract start date, limited to the first quarter only. Anything longer creates precedent and revenue risk.

- Floor evaluation: strongly prefer quarter-end true-up. If Acme insists on monthly true-up, propose a $1,500/month administrative fee to cover invoicing and reconciliation overhead.

- Packaging: add an explicit anti-double-count clause and require the customer to publish the SKU mapping within 30 days of contract signature; Redwood will rely on that mapping for allocation.

Action: Naomi — if you’re comfortable with the fee/term language I’ll incorporate into the Exhibit and return with final tracked redlines.

Ben
Principal, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: legal_clause_proposal.docx (docx)

From: Maya Green <maya.green@acmecloud.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: AcmeCloud Procurement <procure@acmecloud.com>
Date: 2027-05-09T08:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing exhibit redlines and packaging questions

Hi Naomi / Ben — thanks for the quick turnaround. Ben’s language looks reasonable; the account-level cushion definition and the quarter-end true-up are acceptable to Acme, provided we can confirm the 45-day ramp grace-window (we’d prefer 60 days but can live with 45 if necessary).

Two small asks before we wrap:
1) Could you replace the $1,500/month admin fee with a one-time $3,000 onboarding reconciliation fee? That’s easier for our FP&A to model.
2) Please add the PO number (PO-8891) to the order form and include procurement contact (procure@acmecloud.com) on the DocuSign routing.

If you can update the redline and send a DocuSign link today, we’ll aim to return a countersigned copy by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Maya

Attachments: none

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Maya Green <maya.green@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-09T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing exhibit redlines and packaging questions

Maya — great, thanks. We can accept the one-time $3,000 onboarding reconciliation fee in place of the monthly charge. Ben / Laura — I’ll incorporate the $3,000 onboarding fee, lock in the 45-day ramp grace-window, and update Appendix 2 with the anti-double-count language. I’ll also add PO-8891 to the orderform and route the agreement via DocuSign with procurement on the signing order.

I’ll send the DocuSign in ~90 minutes. Proposed timeline:
- Today: Redwood sends updated redline + DocuSign envelope (with PO-8891 and procurement routing).
- Tomorrow EOD: Acme returns countersigned agreement (per Maya).
- Next billing cycle: implement SKU mapping in Appendix 2 and commence quarterly true-ups.

Call if anything changes, otherwise we’ll proceed.

Best,
Naomi
Senior Sales Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: none
